summary: No Blocker. The Phase 11 code and tests match spec FR 1 to FR 8 and decisions K2 to K18. The 88 tests of the clips file pass at the audited head in one heavy-run (exit 0), and the Red 1, Green 1, and mutant captures agree with the plan claims (A5 check clean). No vacuous pass, no digit-only count (A4 and A3 checks clean). Four nonblocking findings: F1 Minor, the mapper copies clips and removes stale clips before it checks the audio block structure and parses the edited week text; F2 to F4 are Nits. The C1 conflict was already decided by the orchestrator; I do not report it.
nonblocking_findings: F1 [Minor] review-a: Section A (code, latent). Location: dashboard/scripts/storytime/set-word-clips.ts:251-283. The mapper copies each bank mp3 and removes stale clips before it reads the audio blocks and parses the edited week text. A week file with a wrong audio block count or an empty audio object gets its clips copied and its stale clips removed, and then the run throws. The state is partial: media writes happened, the week edit did not. A rerun heals it, and the bank checks of C7 run before any write. Spec FR 4 says the script parses the new week text before the first write; the code meets that only for the week-file write. Fix: run the audioBlocks check and parseWeekText of a dry-edited text before the copy loop, or record the order as accepted in the plan.

F2 [Nit] review-a: Section A (code, latent). Location: dashboard/scripts/storytime/set-word-clips.ts:95-96 and :255. The bank fault check tests the mp3 file that the row names (row.mp3), but the copy reads the file at the basename of the planned K3 path. A row whose mp3 value is not wa-<stem>.mp3 passes the fault check, and the copy then fails mid-run, after earlier clips were copied. All 98 shipped rows hold mp3 = wa-<stem>.mp3, so no shipped week is affected. Fix: check the basename file in bankFaultOf too, or compare row.mp3 with the planned basename before any write.

F3 [Nit] review-a: Section A (code, latent). Location: dashboard/scripts/storytime/check-weeks.ts:151-152. checkWordClips records no fault when the bank mp3 named by the row is absent while the week clip exists. The row then passes without the SHA-256 compare against the bank. K12 defines no case for an absent bank mp3 in the check; the mapper catches it, the check does not. Fix: give the check a fail part for a bank mp3 that the row names but the bank does not hold, or record the mapper check as the control.

F4 [Nit] review-a: Section A (mutant coverage). Location: measure/runs/storytime_week_package_20261022/p11-green1-mutants.txt. The 13 caught mutants hold none for these rules: the K4 text edit of editAudioBlock, the K6 append of appendBankRows, the statuses of checkSongLeadIn (K14), the character limit of K11, and the venv stop of K9. Each rule has direct test coverage (C6 asserts the exact 27 added and 2 changed lines and the byte-stable rerun; C14 asserts the append form, the Python form, the char stops, and the venv error; C10 asserts the four statuses of K14), and AC11-9 pins exactly these 13 mutants. So this is a depth note, not a defect. Fix: add one mutant for editAudioBlock and one for appendBankRows to the record of a later phase that touches them.
evidence: HEAD equals cc4f5e67b194848793f7acf3f27d6d37dc751b13 (git rev-parse HEAD and git rev-parse cc4f5e67 give the same SHA), so the audited head is the repository head.

Scope: b27f927f holds only dashboard/__tests__/storytime-package-clips.test.ts; 69cd4db4 holds exactly the 6 allowed files (schema.ts, word-clips.ts, check-weeks.ts, make-word-bank.ts, measure-video-lead-in.ts, set-word-clips.ts); f89a0fff, 49e84ccd, a1fcad97, cc4f5e67 hold only plan.md and measure/runs/ of this track. p11-green1-scope.txt prints files: 6, outside: 0. No content commit exists, and git status holds no change under content/.

Q1 (test quality): the reviewer read all 88 tests of the C1 to C16 cases. Every expected table is written by hand in the file (W01_BOOK0, W01_BOOK1, KEYS_PER_BOOK, FILES_PER_WEEK, W01_TEXT, W01_WEEKS, HEARD_VARIANTS). No assertion sits inside an if that can skip it: the only conditional assertion (line 1750) runs after the status is pinned to pass or warn. C8 case 3 computes the expected exit code from the printed rows, not from the return value, so it is not tautological. C16 holds a real snapshot guard of the content folders. Counts use toBe and toHaveLength, not text scans of digits.

Q1 (A4 fixtures): the reviewer looked for a check that passes on a missing deliverable and found none. The missing-module and missing-export loaders throw (loadModule, exportOf), C7 asserts no file change with tree hashes on three faults, and C12 to C14 assert no write with tree hashes and stamps. No construct-the-missing-deliverable run was needed.

Q2 (mutants): p11-green1-mutants.txt ends with mutants: 13, caught: 13, survivors: none, and restore cmp: all equal. M1 to M13 cover K2 case, K3 stem and path, the K12 SHA compare, the K12 warn and no-row cases, the K13 rounding and second-onset guard, the d=0.05 setting, the K7 peak and edge pad, the mapper write order, the K9 heard rule, and the K15 min(0). The gaps are F4.

Q3 (K12 against K3 and K17): checkWordClips builds the expected path with wordClipPath(week.meta.level, week.meta.week, key) of lib/storytime/word-clips.ts:144-150, which gives l<level>/media/w<nn>/words/wa-<stem>.mp3. It hashes the bank mp3 at run time from the row mp3 value (check-weeks.ts:151-152), not the row WAV hash, as K12 and review F2 require. C9 line 1601-1607 pins that a clip equal to the bank mp3 passes although the row sha256 is the WAV hash. The label matches K12 byte for byte, the row follows family-pictures, the fail parts follow the K12 order, fail wins over warn, and a week with no book or no meta gets no row. checkSongLeadIn matches K14 for all four outcomes.

Q3 (K4 edit): the shipped week files are LF only (grep of carriage returns gives 0), and the two books[].audio blocks sit at indent 6 inside the books array at lines 349 and 980 of w01.json; the meta.audio approval block at line 21 is outside the books range that audioBlocks scans. editAudioBlock returns the opening audio line, and the splice loop keeps the closing line, so the r2 root cause (the dropped audio opening line) cannot repeat. The replace path preserves the trailing comma of the old block. A book with an empty audio object stops the run (F1). The tests pin the exact diff: 27 added lines and 2 changed lines, a byte-stable and time-stable rerun, and a block-only replace.

Q3 (K6 edit): appendBankRows inserts before the last ' ]' line, adds the comma to the last old row, and writes each float with toFixed(1), so -3.0 stays. The tests run the real Python form command on the result (pythonFormHolds, C14 lines 2075 and 2169) and assert one comma line changes.

Q3 (path rules): wordClipPath validates the key against the K2 pattern and the week against 1 to 99, so a planned value cannot leave the content root. The mapper joins values only under contentRoot and reads the bank by basename. The lead-in script joins song paths under contentRoot. No script writes outside its tree in the tests.

Q4 (schema): the diff of schema.ts adds exactly the two optional fields of K15 with JSDoc, wordClips as z.record of the K2 pattern with min(1) values, and videoLeadInSeconds as z.number().finite().min(0). BookAudioSchema and SongSchema stay default z.object (strip, not strict), so the parse keeps the two new fields and a week without them parses as before. The reviewer's heavy-run of the clips file gives 88 passed, exit 0. The PROJECT_TESTS capture p11-green1-project.txt gives 62 files, 1391 tests, exit 0, so the 41 week-parsing test files keep passing.

Q4 (A5, plan claims against captures): p11-red1.txt ends with exit: 1; p11-green1-green.txt gives 4 files, 181 tests, exit 0; p11-green1-project.txt gives 62 files, 1391 tests, exit 0; p11-green1-lint.txt ends with exit: 0; p11-green1-checks.txt gives 0 failed checks, word-clips warn on st2/1 to st2/7 with no clip details, song-lead-in warn on st2/1, no rows on st2/8 and st2/2 to st2/7, and exit: 0; p11-green1-live.txt shows both videos in the r3 MANIFEST, lead-in 3.000 twice, the 12 dry-run keys with chars: 37, and 23 check lines with 11 ok and 12 no bank row. Each value matches the Green 1 task line.

The C1 conflict (a1 and cafe in FR 7 against K2 step 3) was decided by the orchestrator before this review: K2 step 3 is the rule, and the FR 7 example gets a later text fix. The test at lines 1189-1199 follows K2 and documents the deviation. I report no finding for it.
The reviewer ran the clips test file once, in the foreground of one heavy-run wrapper: 1 file, 88 tests, all passed, exit: 0. No PROJECT_TESTS run, no mmx call, no mutant rerun.
